channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Inmate serving life sentence escapes prison
item.description: Jacob Morley, a convicted murderer, escaped from a Tennessee prison on Sunday, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction.

item.title: Trump administration pushes for food assistance card upgrade to fight fraud
item.description: The proposed rule is a major step forward in addressing a form of fraud that has robbed SNAP recipients of millions.

item.title: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
item.description: Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.

item.title: These key Senate races will determine which party controls the body next year
item.description: As both parties prepare for the final leg of the campaign, here are some of the most closely watched Senate races.

item.title: UN cites 'ethnic cleansing' concerns around Israel's Palestinian displacement operation in Hebron
item.description: The United Nations on Monday raised "ethnic cleansing" concerns following Israel's operation to displace by force more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron in the West Bank after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near the city on Friday. UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement that the "aggressive operation" must end, and that "collective punishment is a grave violation of international law".

item.title: French student union leaders call for 'continued mobilisation' after meeting PM
item.description: The French government met student representatives on Monday (October 26) following weeks of unrest. Students who had been demanding a meeting for weeks hail progress. Nonetheless they are now calling for fresh demonstrations next Saturday (October 31) to press for further measures. Details by FRANCE 24’s French Politics Editor Marc Perelman.

item.title: Trump told DOJ to sue to block Alaska Senate results if Republican narrowly loses
item.description: President Trump says he directed the DOJ to preemptively file a lawsuit to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses.

item.title: Brazil: What does Lula's re-election mean for the Amazon?
item.description: Climate activists in Brazil are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. His last four years in power saw a record decrease in deforestation in the world's largest rainforest.

item.title: Opponents accuse Netanyahu of stoking tensions with Iran before Israel's election
item.description: Israel's defence minister denied on Monday (October 26) reports of a rift between PM Netanyahu and the army over Iran, before the vote. Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, insisting only he can "finish the job" in the US-Israeli war on Iran. His main rival, ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, has accused him of playing up the Iran threat when it suits him politically, and of failing to accomplish his war goals. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Pope in 'good health' and trip to South America will go ahead as planned
item.description: The Pope is recovering well from cancer surgery and his trip to South America will go ahead as planned next month, the Vatican has said.

item.title: Leaders across Americas react to Brazil President Lula's re-election
item.description: ​President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential election on Sunday (October 25), defeating right-wing ​Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff to secure a fourth non-consecutive term.

item.title: 'Star Trek' actor Walter Koenig dies at 90
item.description: Walter Koenig's former co-star, George Takei, mourned his death in a Facebook post on Monday.

item.title: Israeli candidate Eisenkot pledges to unite country as Netanyahu deems him 'soft' on Iran
item.description: Israeli presidential candidate Gadi Eisenkot's pledge made Sunday to "heal" Israeli society after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's divisive tenure resonated with some voters attending his final campaign rally before polling begins Tuesday. Netanyahu meanwhile received fresh backing for re-election from US President Donald Trump and deemed Eisenkot "soft" on Iran.

item.title: 'Lula accustomed to negotiating tough bargains': Campaign promises collide with right-wing Congress
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Christopher Sabatini, Director of Chatham House's Latin America Programme. Sabatini examines how Lula's campaign reinvention, youth mobilisation, and the changing dynamics of Bolsonarismo are reshaping Brazil's political landscape. By embracing social media, mobilising younger voters, and shifting attention from his historical achievements to the economic anxieties of ordinary Brazilians, Lula managed to transform the electoral contest. As Sabatini explains, voters were no longer satisfied with hearing about the past. They wanted an answer to a more immediate question: "What are you going to do for us now?

item.title: Israel election: unable to vote from abroad, expats have to fly home
item.description: Israelis can’t vote from abroad, so tens of thousands of expats are expected to fly home for the election. At Tel Aviv airport, supporters of opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot are already waiting at arrivals. A “Fly and Vote” initiative helps expats organise their trip, despite a failed petition from Netanyahu’s Likud party to restrict it. With polls predicting a tight race, every vote could count, and the result will decide the Prime Minister’s fate.

item.title: Why Melania Trump's ceasefire will be lifeline for besieged Ukrainians in Oleshky
item.description: 👉Listen to This Is Why on your podcast app👈

item.title: Macklemore holds charity stadium shows to raise funds for Palestine
item.description: In this arts24 music show, Jennifer Ben Brahim brings us a roundup of the big music releases and news of the week, from US rapper Macklemore's charity stadium shows to raise money for Palestine, to the return of R'n'B crooner John Legend with his 11th album "Muse" – his first collaboration with close friend Pharrell Williams.

item.title: France protests: Macron rules out state of emergency – for now
item.description: The French government sought to draw a line Monday under weeks of protests that have been marred by violence, with President Emmanuel Macron heading to Marseille. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years.

item.title: Lula's re-election brings hope for the Amazon as deforestation drops to record low
item.description: Climate activists in Brazil and beyond are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. His last four years in power saw a record decrease in deforestation in the world's largest rainforest, appropriately nicknamed the planet's lungs. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

item.title: Microsoft offers 'buyouts' to 60,000 staff including UK workers
item.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance packages to 60,000 of its staff - more than a quarter of its workforce - including some in the UK.

item.title: WATCH: Runners take on NYC Marathon with a mission
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer shares the story of “Team Inspire” as they prepare to run 26.2 miles across New York City.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Jordan arrests three following deadly terror attack on church
item.description: Jordanian authorities on Monday arrested three terrorists following a deadly attack on a church during a funeral procession that killed nine people in the western village of Hammoud. The three assailants – who are Islamic extremists, according the Jordanian director of public security – were injured in a dawn shootout with authorities and are due to be brought before the courts in the nation that supports capital punishment.

item.title: Brazil's Lula reelected president in runoff vote: A look back at his career
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday (October 25), the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls.

item.title: US Midterms 2026: A history of gerrymandering
item.description: What does a salamander have to do with US elections? Dating back centuries, gerrymandering continues to play a role in American elections today. Used more often by Republicans in the modern era of voting, Democrats have also resorted to the tactic in the past decade. But what is gerrymandering, and why is it called that? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains.

item.title: Macron promises 'concrete measures' over protest demands - amid fears of Halloween unrest
item.description: Emmanuel Macron says his government will unveil "concrete measures" in response to the demands of student protesters for more resources in France.

item.title: Macron promises 'concrete measures' in response to French students' demands
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said the government would announce “concrete measures" on Monday (October 26) to address school students’ demands after weeks of unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was scheduled to meet with students later Monday. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from the ground.

item.title: US midterms: Obama blasts Trump's 'chaos and cruelty' while campaigning for Democrats
item.description: Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied ‌to White House renovations. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson tells us more.

item.title: Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad expected to fly in for pivotal vote
item.description: Israelis are preparing to head to the polls on Tuesday (October 27). Unable to vote from abroad, tens of thousands of expatriate citizens have been flying in from across the world to cast their ballots. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky met some of them at the airport.

item.title: AI giant Anthropic files for an IPO that could break records
item.description: The AI company, which makes the popular Claude chatbot, has filed for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest ever.

item.title: Man who died after being hit by falling tree in Storm Boelo is named
item.description: Tributes have been paid to a man who died after being struck by a falling tree during Storm Boelo.

item.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to the student-led movement: What's next?
item.description: Serbia's student-led protest movement won a historic victory in parliamentary ⁠election, ending the ​long rule of Aleksandar Vucic and sparking mass celebrations. But their yet-to-be named leaders face a long list of issues. FRANCE 24's Angela Diffley gives us her analysis.

item.title: Lula wins fourth term: What are the reactions in Brazil?
item.description: Brazil's leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva was re-elected against all expectations on Sunday (October 25), but his conservative rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to have the vote annulled. FRANCE 24's Jan Onoszko tells us more.

item.title: WATCH: Obama, Trump rally in battleground state Michigan
item.description: The former and current presidents campaigned for their respective party's candidates in the critical Michigan Senate race.

item.title: Bolsonaro's refusal to concede underscores ‘serious’ challenges to Brazil's democratic institutions
item.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Dr Pedro Perfeito da Silva, Latin American specialist at the University of Exeter. For Dr Perfeito da Silva, Lula's stunning success reflects the convergence of digital organizing, grassroots mobilization, targeted socioeconomic appeals and an effective effort to mobilise opposition to the Bolsonaro political project. As he explains, Lula assembled a coalition that "not only energized his supporters but also attracted voters from groups that had been somewhat skeptical of the government in the first round."

item.title: Will Netanyahu's security promise win him this election?
item.description: Since the beginning of his political career, Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, has campaigned on a promise that he is the only one who will keep the Jewish state safe. As Israelis head to the polls for their first election since the October7 Hamas attacks and the start of the war in Gaza, Netanyahu's strategy might be less effective. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler explains.

item.title: Lula wins Brazil election but faces uphill battle to govern
item.description: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's narrow election victory on Sunday has dealt a blow to Brazil's far right, but deep political divisions remain. The newly re-elected president must tackle economic and security concerns at home while navigating international tensions with US President Donald Trump.

item.title: WATCH: Homeowners go all out with Halloween decorations
item.description: Front yards are being transformed into Halloween spectacles, with the elaborate decorations lifting spirits.

item.title: Australian judge rejects prisoner's human rights challenge to Vegemite ban
item.description: Andre McKechnie, 55, is serving a life sentence for murder. He took his battle for the salty, sticky, black-brown byproduct of brewing beer to the court last year. He argued being refused Vegemite breached the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act.

item.title: What to know about China's plenum as Xi seeks stronger party discipline
item.description: This closed-door gathering that started Monday comes about a year before Xi is expected to secure a fourth term and personnel changes to key leadership bodies.

item.title: Belgrade in rapture as Serbian students topple Vucic in historic election
item.description: Serbia's student-led movement declared victory in parliamentary elections Sunday ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist party. Vucic conceded defeat less than two hours after polls closed, triggering raucous scenes in the capital as supporters of the movement celebrated the defeat of a government they blamed for deep-rooted corruption.

item.title: Anthropic reveals plans for blockbuster IPO
item.description: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic, the company behind the popular Claude chatbot, has filed papers to sell shares to the public for the first time.

item.title: Drivers who killed mother and young daughter as they raced are jailed
item.description: Two strangers who killed a mother and her four-year-old daughter as they raced their high-performance cars along a city centre road have been jailed for 16 and 12 years.

item.title: Live: French student representatives hail ‘concrete measures’, call for protests to continue
item.description: Representatives from French high school student groups on Monday hailed the government’s first measures to calm the crisis over ongoing unrest linked to their protest movement, including a gradual replacement of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup, but called for “continued mobilisation” after their meeting with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. Follow our liveblog for all the latest.
